_instructions: Fill in `plan` and `workouts` below with the real half marathon training plan data.
workouts must contain exactly 5, 6 or 7 rows per week (however many training days per week the plan actually has) x however many weeks the plan runs.
date is ISO format YYYY-MM-DD, one row per real calendar day the plan schedules a session.
week is the week number (1, 2, 3...), matching the *.webp week-banner files already on disk.

phase is a short label shown as a tag on the week tile, e.g. 'Base Phase', 'Build Phase', 'Peak Phase', 'Taper Phase' -- reuse this same small set of phase names across weeks, don't invent a unique phase per week.

cover_url must be one of the three existing session photos: assets/photos/half-marathon/easy-run.webp, assets/photos/half-marathon/long-run.webp, or assets/photos/half-marathon/quality-run.webp -- pick whichever best matches that session's intensity (easy run = easy-run.webp, long steady run = long-run.webp, intervals/tempo/race-pace = quality-run.webp). If a session is genuinely not a run (e.g. a rest or cross-training day), skip that row entirely -- only real training-day workouts belong in this file, not rest days.

week_cover_url is only set on the FIRST workout of each week (by date) -- set it to assets/photos/half-marathon/half-marathon-week-<N>.webp for that one row, and leave it null on every other workout that same week.
discipline is a JSON object describing the structured session shown on the workout's detail screen. Shape:
metric: { kind: 'duration' | 'distance', value: '<display string, e.g. "40 min" or "8 km">' } -- REQUIRED, this is the pill shown at the top of the screen.

target: { label: '<e.g. "Target pace" or "Target effort">', value: '<e.g. "5:30 /km" or "RPE 6/10">' } -- OPTIONAL, omit entirely (don't include the key) if there's no specific target for this session.

warmup, mainSet, cooldown: plain instructional sentences, each OPTIONAL (omit the key if not applicable). Write these as clear coaching instructions in the app's own voice (e.g. '10 min easy jogging.' / '5 x 1km at target pace, 2 min recovery jog between reps.'), not pasted verbatim from a spreadsheet's casual notes.
estimate_minutes is a rough whole-number duration for the session in minutes (used only as a fallback label on the Week screen row, alongside the photo).
title is the short session name shown throughout the app, e.g. 'Easy Run', 'Long Run', 'Quality Run', 'Race-Pace Run'.
summary is one sentence shown just under the title on the workout's detail screen, describing the session's purpose in plain language.
session is a legacy fallback field -- leave it null on every row (discipline is what actually renders; session is only used if discipline is entirely missing, which should never happen here).

workouts._example: One example row shown for shape reference -- delete this key and replace the array with all real rows for every week.
workouts.title: Easy Run
workouts.summary: An easy, conversational-pace run to build aerobic base without adding fatigue.

discipline.mainSet: Easy, continuous running at a conversational effort.
